issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a PersonService method named addParent(Person person, Person parent) to be implemented, but the solution implementation provides a method named registerParent(Person person, Person parent) instead. PersonResource (and tests) call personService.addParent(...). This name mismatch between the expected method (addParent) and the solution's registerParent will cause confusion and compilation errors if students compare or use the solution code directly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's service API match the specification and template by renaming registerParent(...) to addParent(...) (keeping the same parameters and behavior). Alternatively, add an addParent(Person, Person) delegating method that calls registerParent(...) so PersonResource and tests can use addParent as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a PersonService method named addParent(Person person, Person parent). In the solution implementation the corresponding method is named registerParent(...) instead of addParent(...). Meanwhile other artifacts (PersonResource and tests) still call addParent(...). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (adding a parent relation) creates a mapping barrier for students and can lead to compilation/runtime confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the operation across all artifacts. Rename the solution method registerParent(...) to addParent(...), or add a delegating addParent(...) method that calls registerParent(...). Ensure tests and PersonResource refer to the same method name (addParent).
